- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of forecast horizon).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then gradually decline, while true outcomes often show sharper, delayed peaks or more volatile corrections.
- Model fails to capture mean reversion in the short term — prices often overshoot recent highs and then drop more than expected.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of price spikes in the middle of the forecast horizon (e.g., around day 10–15).
- Model shows persistent upward bias in the first 5–7 days, then gradually flattens — true outcomes often show a sharper downward correction after a peak.
- Model does not adjust for recent volatility or sudden policy changes — true outcomes often react more aggressively to external shocks than model predicts.
- Model tends to smooth out volatility, leading to underestimation of sharp drops or spikes in the final 5–10 days of the forecast.
- Model overconfident in linear trends — fails to account for non-linear corrections or sudden reversals after spikes.
